subject: Tri-region technical deep-dive — coordinating a 90m overlap window
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finovate.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finovate.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, ava.chen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tri-region technical deep-dive — coordinating a 90m overlap window

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the intro call last week. Per our discussion, the next step is a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive (Solutions Engineer + your platform + architects) to walk through architecture, integration points, and performance expectations. We want to make sure we have the right folks from both sides online for the whole session.

We realize mixing US / EU / APAC calendars is painful, so I ran a quick pass on candidate windows anchored in UTC. Can you please indicate which (if any) work for your team, and whether any of your architects need earlier/later options? We can also split into two shorter region-specific sessions, but prefer one full overlap if possible.

Candidate 90m windows (times shown in local example + UTC):
- Option A: 15 Sep, 16:00–17:30 UTC (US PDT 09:00–10:30, EU CEST 18:00–19:30, APAC IST 21:30–23:00)
- Option B: 16 Sep, 13:00–14:30 UTC (US PDT 06:00–07:30, EU CEST 15:00–16:30, APAC SGT 21:00–22:30)
- Option C: 17 Sep, 18:00–19:30 UTC (US PDT 11:00–12:30, EU CEST 20:00–21:30, APAC AEST 05:00–06:30 next day)

Notes: 1) We used UTC anchor to avoid DST confusion — if you have fixed office locations, tell us the preferred local zone. 2) If any option crosses into on-call boundaries for your engineers, we can shift +/- 30m. 3) Attached: a proposed agenda and a .ics to drop into calendars.

Agenda draft attached — please suggest additions.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tri-region technical deep-dive — coordinating a 90m overlap window

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the UTC anchor, that helps. Quick notes from our side:

- We need at least three of our architects: myself (Dublin), Priya (London), and Amit Shah (Bengaluru). Amit is UTC+5:30 — late evenings there are OK but prefer not to push past 23:00 local.
- Option A looks promising for us but could be tight for Amit (21:30 IST start). Option B lands at 21:00 SGT for our APAC person — workable but right at the edge.
- Option C is tough because it hits AEST early morning and Amit would be on call.

Could we try for Option A but shift start 30 minutes earlier (15:30–17:00 UTC) so Amit starts at 21:00 IST and EU folks finish at 19:00 CEST? That keeps US at 08:30 PDT which Jordan might prefer earlier.

Also — quick heads up: EU clocks are stable through September; our APAC team has a local holiday block on 18–19 Sep, so anything 17th onward will be unreliable.

Liam

Hi Liam / Rishi —

Thanks for the context, Liam. A few practical constraints from SE side:
- Our lead SE (Ava) is available 08:00–12:00 PDT that week; Jordan can shift earlier if needed but asked to avoid before 07:30 PDT.
- We prefer starting on a half-hour boundary when mixing IST offsets (makes conversions simpler).

If the team is happy to try a 90m at 15:30–17:00 UTC on 15 Sep (per Liam's suggestion shifted 30m earlier), practical local times are:
- US (PDT): 08:30–10:00
- EU (CEST): 17:30–19:00 — note EU folks asked to finish by 19:00 local; this meets that.
- IST: 21:00–22:30 — keeps Amit at 21:00 start, under his 23:00 cutoff.

I'll drop a provisional calendar hold for Rishi/Ava/Jordan and include the agenda + required infra diagram. If anyone needs to swap out the 90m for two 45m focused sessions, say so now.

— Soojin
